source_exclusions.reason: manually reviewed one-source-frame robot insert that creates a two-project-frame flash before the intended wide action shot

reviewed_music_events.role: first lift: move from the established workshop team into a closer view of their work or weapon
commitment: move from setup into unmistakable threat or action
climax drive: begin the strongest sustained action and complete its visual peak before frame 375
release: cut away from action to a held low-motion aftermath, survivor, or environmental resolution

story_brief: Recut one visual world into a concise action trailer: open inside the workshop on the human team and the same machine or weapon that drives the following shots, move closer into their work, reveal the mechanical threat, build into the strongest sustained action during frames 249..375, then cut away from all action at frame 375 to a held low-motion resolution during the musical decay. The opening cannot introduce a visually isolated armored character, balcony, or location that the remaining four shots abandon. The first shot must make shot two feel like a closer continuation of the same team, room, or device. The fourth shot must carry the climax and the fifth must release it; do not place fighting, firing, collision, or major robot movement under the final fade. Every hard cut must have clean incoming handles, and the release must use a composition distinct enough from the outgoing climax that it cannot read as a temporal stutter. Every selected shot must advance that same conflict. The reviewed musical events are editorial targets, not interchangeable metronome ticks. There is no second source quota and no parallel-world conceit.
